messages:
incident-bot: 🚨 INCIDENT: inference-api p99 spike and streaming stalls detected across us-west — SLO breach. Alerts from synthetic checks and customer reports.
lia: seeing a big tail on streaming connections for /v1/generate — p95 ~450ms -> 2.1s, p99 ~1.8s -> 8.5s. Affects hosted tier + some Dedicated nodes in us-west.
kevin: confirmed. Traces point to control-plane config fetch (feature-flag) calls and auth token lookups. Increased retries on clients.
ani: customer impact note: multiple customers reporting intermittent streaming disconnects, some client SDKs retrying aggressively. Potentially billing churn risk.
raj: piling logs: auth service latency 95th -> 700ms, token-store DB CPU spike, redis rate-limiter queueing.
sre-jamie: running `kubectl get pods -n controlplane` shows restart churn for `config-fetcher-v2` 2/3 pods OOMKilled in last 10m.
kevin: can we temporarily route streaming auth to fallback token cache? Is there a feature-flag we can flip to bypass fresh token validation? @deploy-bot any quick options?
deploy-bot: quick rollback available: `ff:configfetch_v2 -> off` will flip to v1 cached path. Canary rollout at 10% ready. Use `./ops/ff-toggle --env=prod --flag=configfetch_v2 --off --reason="inc auth latency"`.
lia: doing the flip now on us-west canary. Will watch synthetic.
lia: ✅ flipped canary. synthetic streaming p99 dropped from 8.5s -> 3.2s on canary. Still high in main cluster.
ani: we should also raise read replicas for token-store DB. DB CPU sustained at 92% on primary.
raj: spinning up an extra read replica, but the token-store writes still contend. Adding read replica reduces auth read latency for cached tokens.
sre-jamie: added replica, rebalanced read traffic. auth p95 dropped to ~220ms on canary. p99 still ~900ms overall.
kevin: root cause draft: recent configfetch_v2 change increased on-demand feature-flag fetches per request; combined with stricter auth validation and client retries, causing token-store pressure and rate-limiter queueing -> tail latency.
product-maya: which customers are impacted? any high-value ones hitting errors?
ani: lists: two enterprise accounts saw streaming disconnects (support ticket ids 4512, 4521). No billing anomalies yet but UX regressions.
lia: mitigation plan (short): 1) keep configfetch_v2 off globally for us-west, 2) enable short-term fail-open for auth validation for streaming requests (skip fresh validation if cached token less than 1m old), 3) increase rate-limiter window and throttle low-priority clients.
kevin: can we fail-open safely? we'll log and tail for violations. Implement via gateway rule: `if request.type==streaming & token.age<60s -> accept`
raj: pushed gateway change to us-west as a hotfix. syntax: ```yaml
- match: request.type==streaming
  condition: token.age_seconds < 60
  action: bypass-auth-validation
```
lia: toggled global configfetch_v2 -> off for us-west. Observability: streaming p99 down to 420ms, client retries reduced by ~70%.
ani: continuing customer comms: pinged affected accounts with interim workaround and ETA.
product-maya: please draft post-incident note for impacted customers: root cause, what we changed, ETA for permanent fix.
sre-jamie: next steps (medium): audit configfetch_v2 memory usage and add backpressure on feature-flag fetcher; add KV local cache for token validation path; increase token-store write capacity and add slower-path bulk backoff on client retries.
kevin: I'll open a PR to add a token LRU cache in gateway and rate-limit spike detector to avoid client retry storms.
lia: handing off to oncall-night: @raj you'll be primary for next 8h. Keep configfetch_v2 off until PR validated.
raj: ack, taking handoff. I'll monitor `auth.token_store.latency`, `gateway.stream_disconnects`, and `configfetch.errors`.
lia: summary for handoff: what we flipped, what to watch, customer tickets. Saved snippet: ```
- FF: configfetch_v2 -> OFF (us-west)
- Gateway hotfix: streaming token age bypass enabled
- DB: +1 read replica added to token-store
- Active alerts: auth.p99, gateway.stream_disconnects > 0.5%
```
ani: leaving notes in pagerduty incident and updating triage board. If p99 goes above 1s for >5m, escalate to SEV-1.
product-maya: thanks — coordinate a follow-up postmortem and impact classification (SEV-2 current, could escalate).
raj: will own stabilization and follow-up. ping me for access.
incident-bot: Incident updated: status=mitigated, assignee=raj, severity=SEV-2. Next update due in 2h. :white_check_mark:
